question: Who should standard precautions apply to in the hospital?

options.A: Patients admitted through the emergency department
options.B: Only patients diagnosed with active tuberculosis
options.C: Only those showing visible signs of infection
options.D: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis

explanation: We treat everyone with standard precautions because we never know who might be carrying an infection, keeping both you and your patients safe! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind using standard precautions?

options.A: Body fluids from any patient may harbor infectious agents
options.B: Only surgical patients require active barrier protection
options.C: Infection risk is zero until laboratory tests confirm disease
options.D: Healthy individuals cannot transmit hospital pathogens

explanation: Always assume any patient's blood or body fluids could carry germs. It's the golden rule of staying safe on the ward! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: When must you wash your hands with soap and water instead of using an alcohol rub?

options.A: Before touching a patient with intact skin
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: Every time you exit a standard medical ward
options.D: After taking a patient's temperature with an oral thermometer

explanation: If your hands look dirty or have body fluids on them, alcohol won't cut it. Soap, water, and good friction are needed to wash the dirt away! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: How are transient skin germs different from your normal resident skin germs?

options.A: Resident flora live only on the outer surface and cause rapid infections
options.B: Transient flora are acquired through contact and easily removed by hand hygiene
options.C: Resident flora are eliminated by standard alcohol rubs in seconds
options.D: Transient flora permanently colonize deep skin layers

explanation: Transient germs are just hitchhikers you picked up from touching things around the ward. A good hand wash easily washes them away! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which piece of PPE should you take off first when doffing?
explanation: Your gloves get the most exposed to germs, so you take them off first so you don't accidentally spread anything to your clean clothes or face. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: Why should you only touch the straps when handling a used face mask?

options.A: Touching the filter fabric alters the breathing resistance
options.B: The front surface collects pathogens and droplets during care
options.C: The straps contain the antimicrobial coating
options.D: Elastic bands break easily if pulled from the center

explanation: The front of the mask catches all the germs and droplets, so always use the straps to keep your fingers clean! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do after using a disposable injection needle?

options.A: Recap it carefully using both hands to prevent spills
options.B: Break the needle off to fit more items in the bin
options.C: Place it on the bedside tray until the procedure is finished
options.D: Drop it directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container

explanation: Never delay! Drop used sharps straight into the safety box to avoid accidental pricks. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is using both hands to recap a used needle dangerous?

options.A: It increases the chance of missing the cap and puncturing the hand
options.B: It damages the sharp tip making subsequent injections painful
options.C: It violates sterility standards for the medication vial
options.D: It prevents proper activation of built-in safety shields

explanation: Trying to guide a cap onto a needle with two hands is a recipe for an accidental needle-stick injury. Safety first: don't recap when you don't have to! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: What should you do if you need to sneeze and have no tissue nearby?

options.A: Cover your mouth with both bare hands
options.B: Turn away and sneeze directly into open air
options.D: Hold the sneeze in by pinching your nose

explanation: Sneezing into your elbow keeps germs off your hands, preventing you from spreading them to door handles and patients! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why do hospitals place hand sanitizers and masks right at the entrance?

options.A: To encourage immediate containment by people with respiratory symptoms
options.B: To comply with fire safety regulations for waiting areas
options.C: To allow staff to clean their shoes before entering wards
options.D: To test the water supply pressure for facility audits

explanation: Catching coughs and sanitizing hands right at the door stops germs from traveling deeper into the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: What must you do before putting a disinfectant chemical on a very dirty surface?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly
options.B: Seal the room off for twenty-four hours
options.C: Clean the surface to remove organic soil
options.D: Spray alcohol over the top and let it dry instantly

explanation: Dirt and blood can block disinfectants from working properly. Always clean the surface first, then disinfect! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why does the manufacturer give a specific 'contact time' for surface disinfectants?

options.A: It allows the housekeeping staff to track their working hours
options.B: It ensures the chemical remains wet long enough to kill pathogens
options.C: It prevents the plastic casing from melting under heat
options.D: It guarantees that the spray bottle will not leak

explanation: Disinfectants need time to do their job! Keeping the surface wet for the recommended minutes guarantees the germs are actually dead. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after a needlestick injury?

options.A: Fill out the institutional incident report form online
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the puncture wound
options.C: Search for the patient's chart to check their diagnosis
options.D: Wash the exposed site immediately with soap and water

explanation: Don't panic! Immediately wash the spot with soap and water to rinse away as much of the contaminant as possible. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why must an accidental needle prick be reported right away?

options.A: Laboratory tests on the worker take several days to process
options.B: Hospital insurance policies expire after two hours
options.C: Post-exposure prophylaxis is most effective when started quickly
options.D: The nurse cannot leave the shift without an official note

explanation: Getting help fast means protective medications can be started early if needed, keeping you safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)
